findings.title: Dedup drops a genuinely different KOT ticket (different print_jobs id) for the same order+printer while the first is still in flight
findings.detail: enqueue() collapses any job with the same orderId+ackType+printerId that is pending/processing/retrying and returns the existing job's id with ok:true. But every job arriving here has already been CLAIMED on the server (printGateway.ts / usePrintJobBridge.ts claim before calling electronAPI.print) and carries its own print_jobs.jobId. The server only creates a second KOT job for an order when there is a real new delta (commitKotState runs at dispatch, so a true double-tap yields no_delta and no job), so a second job is different content (e.g. item B added after item A). The dropped job is never printed, never acked and never released: it sits 'claimed' until the 2-minute stale window, and the host only re-polls pending jobs on mount/reconnect.
findings.failure_scenario: Staff taps KOT for table 5 (adds Paneer); while that ticket is printing or retrying (printer slow / offline, retries take up to ~17 s) they add Butter Naan and tap KOT again. Server creates job #2 for the Naan delta, the host claims it, enqueue() dedups it into job #1 and returns ok. The kitchen never gets the Naan ticket, and the POS shows 'KOT sent to printer'.
findings.suggested_fix: When spec.printJob.jobId is present, dedup only on the same jobId (that is the true duplicate key). Keep the order+type+printer heuristic only for jobs with no server jobId.

findings.title: Main-process printer config is cached forever; edits made from any other device never reach the print queue
findings.detail: getPrinters() caches printSettings.printers in printerCache after the first successful fetch and only clears it on IPC REFRESH_PRINTERS, whose only caller is PrintSettingsPanel on THIS Electron window. The renderer (usePrintJobBridge/printGateway) decides what to claim from the fresh /api/settings query, but executePrintJob resolves the printer from the stale main-process cache.
findings.failure_scenario: Owner adds a new category-routed printer (or re-detects a Windows queue name / changes a network printer IP) from the phone on Vercel. The shop PC's renderer sees the new config and claims the job, but executor throws 'Printer "p-new" not found in settings' (or sends to the old IP/queue), retries 3 times, releases it, and the ticket is not printed until the Electron app is restarted.
findings.suggested_fix: Give printerCache a short TTL (e.g. 60 s) and, in executePrintJob's not-found path, invalidate the cache and refetch once before failing; or have the renderer pass the printer config it validated along with the job.

findings.title: Reconnect creates a new ZkAdapter without disconnecting the previous one
findings.detail: reconcile() sets connected=false on any getAttendances() failure and, on the next cycle, connect() overwrites this.adapter with a new ZkAdapter. The old adapter (still holding an open TCP session to the device and its getRealTimeLogs listener) is never disconnected. Likewise a connect() that loses the 10 s timeout race leaves the pending zk socket un-destroyed. ZKTeco devices typically accept only one concurrent TCP session.
findings.failure_scenario: The K30 is busy for one sync (getAttendances throws once). Every following reconcile opens a new session while the old one still holds the device; the new connects time out, the panel shows 'Last error: Timed out connecting' indefinitely and live punches from the orphaned session keep firing duplicate flushes. While the device is unreachable for a day, one orphaned ZKLib/socket is created per sync interval.
findings.suggested_fix: In connect(), `await this.adapter?.disconnect().catch(() => {})` before creating the new adapter; in ZkAdapter.connect(), call disconnect() when the timeout wins and clear the timer when createSocket wins.

findings.title: start() check-then-act: concurrent start (bootstrap timer vs ATTENDANCE_REFRESH, or two refreshes) runs two agents
findings.detail: start() tests `this.running` before awaiting getConfig() and sets it only afterwards, so two overlapping start() calls both proceed, each creating an adapter and a pair of setIntervals; reconcileTimer/flushTimer are overwritten so stop() can no longer clear the first pair or disconnect the first adapter.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin clicks Save on the Device panel twice quickly (or saves just as the 30 s bootstrap timer fires): two reconcile/flush loops and two device sessions run for the rest of the app session; refresh/stop never stops the orphaned one.
findings.suggested_fix: Set a `starting` flag (or store the in-flight start promise) before the first await and return it to concurrent callers; serialize restart().

findings.title: Overlapping flush() calls slice the buffer by their own batch length, dropping unsent punches
findings.detail: flush() can run concurrently (15 s timer, live-punch flush, reconcile flush, setImmediate continuation). Each takes slice(0,200) and on success does buffer = buffer.slice(batch.length) without checking what is still at the head. Two flushes sending the same first 200 both remove 200, so the second removes 200 punches that were never sent if a third (continuation) flush carrying them then fails.
findings.failure_scenario: After an outage the buffer has 250 punches; timer flush A and reconcile flush B both send the first 200. A succeeds (50 left, continuation C sends them), B succeeds and empties the buffer, C fails on a network blip: the last 50 punches are gone and the cursor is already past them, so reconcile never re-sends them.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard flush() with an in-flight flag (or promise) so only one runs at a time, and remove sent punches by identity rather than by count.

findings.title: Embedded server restart budget (5) is per app lifetime and has no backoff
findings.detail: serverRestarts is never reset after a healthy run and the respawn is immediate. The host build is meant to be the always-on WhatsApp/print host left open for days; after the 5th crash in total (even weeks apart), the embedded server is never restarted while the window keeps pointing at the dead http://localhost:5179. A crash-on-boot (bad host-config DATABASE_URL, port in use) also burns all 5 restarts in a few seconds.
findings.failure_scenario: Host PC runs for two weeks; the server child crashes 5 times on transient DB errors. The 6th crash leaves the POS UI and Baileys dead with only a console warning until someone restarts the app.
findings.suggested_fix: Reset serverRestarts after the child has been up for a few minutes, add exponential backoff between respawns, and surface a dialog/notification when giving up.

findings.title: No setWindowOpenHandler/will-navigate: wa.me and other external links open as Electron windows inheriting the app preload
findings.detail: The app calls window.open for https://wa.me/... in several places (utils/whatsapp.ts, POS.tsx, AutomationPanel.tsx, Reports.tsx). With no webContents.setWindowOpenHandler, Electron creates a child BrowserWindow with the parent's webPreferences (including preload.cjs), so the third-party wa.me / api.whatsapp.com page gets window.electronAPI (print arbitrary ESC/POS, set print-station config, USB scan, attendance test). It also means WhatsApp opens inside an unauthenticated Electron window instead of the user's browser/WhatsApp app.
findings.failure_scenario: Staff clicks 'Send WhatsApp' in Customers on the shop PC: an Electron window opens on whatsapp.com instead of WhatsApp Desktop, with electronAPI exposed to that remote origin.
findings.suggested_fix: Add mainWindow.webContents.setWindowOpenHandler: allow about:blank (the print-fallback popup) and send any http(s) URL to shell.openExternal with { action: 'deny' }; add a will-navigate guard for off-app URLs.

findings.title: normalizePhone uses startsWith("91") — the bug CLAUDE.md says was fixed server-side still lives in the client wa.me path
findings.detail: A real 10-digit mobile starting with 91 (e.g. 9187654321) is left at 10 digits and rejected as invalid; an 11-digit number with a trunk 0 (09876543210) becomes 9109876543210 (13 digits) and passes the length check, opening wa.me with a wrong number. The only caller (CustomerDashboard.tsx handleSendWA) ignores the returned { success:false } and shows the 'sent' state anyway.
findings.failure_scenario: Owner taps Thank You for a customer whose phone is 9187654321: nothing opens but the button flips to 'sent'. For 09876543210 WhatsApp opens on a non-existent number.
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror normalizeWaPhone's length-based rule (10 → prepend 91, 11 with leading 0 → strip and prepend, 12 starting 91 → keep), and have the caller show an error when success is false.

findings.title: 'Cannot delete a table with an active order' is a client-only check on possibly stale data
findings.detail: handleDelete checks table.status from the cached /api/tables list (15 s fallback poll), and DELETE /api/tables/:id (requireAuth only) unconditionally deletes the row via storage.deleteTable with no status/currentOrderId check. Any logged-in staff session can delete any table.
findings.failure_scenario: A waiter opens an order on T4 from a phone; within the poll window the manager on the PC still sees T4 as free and deletes it. The table row (and its currentOrderId link) is gone while the order is still open, so the running bill no longer appears on the Tables page.
findings.suggested_fix: Server-side: refuse delete (409) when the table is not free or has a currentOrderId, ideally in the DELETE's WHERE clause, and gate table create/edit/delete to manager/admin.

findings.title: Shift/Edit/Delete controls are opacity-0 until hover — invisible on touch and keyboard, but still clickable
findings.detail: The action bar uses opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100 with no focus-within/touch alternative. On phones/tablets there is no visible way to shift a table, and the invisible buttons still receive taps.
findings.failure_scenario: A staff member on a phone taps the lower-right of a free table card to open it and instead triggers the 'Delete table?' confirm or the Shift PIN prompt; Shift Table is otherwise undiscoverable on touch.
findings.suggested_fix: Show the bar on focus-within and on touch devices (e.g. @media (hover: none) opacity-100), or move these actions into a long-press / overflow menu.

findings.title: libusb bulk transfer has no timeout — a stalled printer wedges the whole print queue (macOS/Linux hosts)
findings.detail: outEndpoint.transfer is awaited with the endpoint's default timeout (0 = unlimited in node-usb/libusb). PrintQueue processes one job at a time (processing=true) and has no per-job timeout, so a printer that stops accepting data (paper out, cover open, cable glitch mid-job) leaves the promise pending forever.
findings.failure_scenario: On a Mac thin client the USB thermal printer runs out of paper mid-ticket: the transfer never completes, every later KOT/Bill sits 'pending' in the local queue (already claimed on the server), and nothing prints until the app is restarted.
findings.suggested_fix: Set outEndpoint.timeout (e.g. 10 s) before transfer, and wrap execute() in PrintQueue with an overall timeout so a hung job fails into the normal retry/release path.

findings.title: Test print double-centres lines and formats time with the PC's ambient timezone
findings.detail: buildTestBuffer issues E.ALIGN_CENTER then E.centered(..., W) (CLAUDE.md: never combine, it double-centres and drifts), and uses new Date().toLocaleString('en-IN') instead of formatISTDateTime.
findings.failure_scenario: The test ticket's printer name/time/message lines print shifted right of the 'TEST PRINT' heading, and on a PC not set to IST shows the wrong time.
findings.suggested_fix: Use E.line() under ALIGN_CENTER and formatISTDateTime() from shared/print/formatDate.ts.

findings.title: Postgres TLS certificate verification disabled
findings.detail: ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: false } encrypts but does not authenticate the Supabase server, so anyone able to intercept the connection (shop LAN for the Electron host build, any on-path network) can present their own cert and read the DATABASE_URL credentials and all data.
findings.failure_scenario: The embedded host build on the restaurant Wi-Fi connects through a hostile/compromised router performing TLS interception; the DB password and every query are exposed without any error.
findings.suggested_fix: Ship Supabase's CA certificate (ssl: { ca, rejectUnauthorized: true }) or use sslmode=verify-full.
